headline.headline: DELAUTER'S NIGHTMARE IN RIGHT FIELD SWINGS ALCS BACK TO EVEN
headline.deck: Rays capitalize on costly seventh-inning error to take Game 4, 7-3
headline.body:
CLEVELAND — Chase DeLauter's misplay in right field in the seventh inning unraveled what had been a competitive ballgame Saturday afternoon at Progressive Field, and the Tampa Bay Rays seized the opportunity without hesitation, scoring three runs in the frame to turn a tight contest into a 7-3 victory over the Cleveland Guardians and level the American League Championship Series at two games apiece.

The Rays trailed 1-0 after the first inning before clawing back to tie it in the third. Tampa Bay added a run in the sixth, but it was the seventh that broke Cleveland's spirit. The Rays pushed across three runs in that frame, the rally sustained by DeLauter's error in right that kept the inning alive when the Guardians needed an out most. Junior Caminero, Yandy Diaz and Jonathan Aranda combined for six hits in 14 at-bats and drove in five of the seven Tampa Bay runs, providing the offensive muscle that winning pitcher N. Martinez needed to secure the decision in front of 33,355 fans at Progressive Field.

Tampa Bay tacked on two more insurance runs in the ninth to set the final at 7-3. The series now shifts back to Tampa with the best-of-seven tied, two games apiece, and a Cleveland club that watched its two-game advantage dissolve in the span of 48 hours. Game 5 is scheduled for Monday night in St. Petersburg.

secondary.headline: JOHN BEAKE, ARCHITECT OF THE ELWAY TRADE, DEAD AT 87
secondary.deck: Former Broncos executive helped build two Super Bowl champions in Denver
secondary.body:
John Beake, the former Denver Broncos executive whose backroom maneuvering helped engineer the blockbuster 1983 trade that brought quarterback John Elway to Denver and set the franchise on the path to back-to-back Super Bowl championships, died Saturday at the age of 87. Beake spent years in the Broncos' front office and was widely regarded as one of the more underappreciated architects of the franchise's golden era.

Elway, acquired from the Baltimore Colts in what remains one of the most consequential trades in NFL history, led Denver to Super Bowl titles in the 1997 and 1998 seasons. Beake was instrumental in making that future possible, and his fingerprints were on the personnel decisions that surrounded Elway throughout the quarterback's Hall of Fame career. The Broncos organization and the broader NFL community mourned his passing Saturday.

secondary.headline: DYBANTSA ANKLE INJURY PUTS WIZARDS ON EDGE BEFORE OPENER
secondary.deck: No. 1 overall pick exits preseason finale after awkward landing in Washington
secondary.body:
WASHINGTON — AJ Dybantsa, the first overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft and the centerpiece of the Washington Wizards' rebuild, exited the franchise's preseason finale Saturday after rolling his ankle on an awkward landing, throwing the team's immediate outlook into uncertainty just days before the regular season opens. The severity of the injury was not immediately confirmed, but the sight of Dybantsa limping from the floor alarmed a fan base that has waited years for a reason for optimism.

The Wizards have not yet classified Dybantsa's status for opening night. The injury arrives as other franchises in the Eastern Conference are finalizing their own rosters: the New York Knicks announced they are waiving guard Bruce Brown while retaining center James Wiseman, and the Philadelphia 76ers converted seven-foot-six center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract to address a mounting frontcourt injury situation. The East is very much in flux as the regular season approaches.

secondary.headline: LEHKONEN'S TWO-GOAL GAME POWERS AVALANCHE PAST FLYERS
secondary.deck: Colorado continues strong second-round push as Philadelphia sinks deeper into trouble
secondary.body:
Artturi Lehkonen delivered a two-goal performance to propel the Colorado Avalanche past the Philadelphia Flyers in their most recent meeting, giving the Avalanche a 5-2-1 record and keeping them firmly in the hunt during the second round of the NHL playoffs. Philadelphia, at 1-6-3, has become one of the more troubled teams in the Metropolitan Division, and another loss to a Western Conference power only deepened the gloom around the organization.

Colorado's visit to Philadelphia followed a stretch in which the Avalanche demonstrated the kind of two-way game that makes them dangerous in the postseason bracket. Lehkonen, a reliable performer in high-stakes hockey dating back to his Stanley Cup run with Colorado in 2022, again proved himself a clutch contributor. The Flyers, by contrast, have managed only one win in ten outings and face serious questions about whether the roster can stabilize before the season spirals further out of reach.

column.headline: CLEVELAND HAD THE RAYS RIGHT WHERE THEY WANTED THEM — THEN GAVE IT BACK
column.body:
Two games up in the American League Championship Series, playing at home, holding a lead into the late innings — the Cleveland Guardians had constructed as favorable a position as a team can build in October baseball. Then Chase DeLauter's glove failed him in the seventh inning Saturday, and just like that, all that careful construction came down like a house of cards in a stiff breeze off Lake Erie. That is the cruel arithmetic of playoff baseball: one misplay, one moment of imprecision, and the entire ledger resets.

The Rays are not a team that requires a formal invitation. Junior Caminero and Yandy Diaz and Jonathan Aranda are professional hitters who have earned their roster spots through work, and when a door opens, they walk through it. Tampa Bay came into Progressive Field needing two wins to save their season and now leaves having taken both of them. The ALCS is tied. The momentum, such as it is, has crossed the state of Ohio heading southwest toward Florida. Cleveland had the Rays cornered, and the Rays got out anyway. That should alarm everyone inside the Guardians' clubhouse.

story.headline: RAYS EVEN ALCS AT 2-2 WITH 7-3 WIN OVER GUARDIANS
story.deck: Tampa Bay erupts for five seventh-inning runs to stun Cleveland in Game 4
story.body:
CLEVELAND — The seventh inning turned this American League Championship Series upside down Saturday afternoon. Tampa Bay trailed the Guardians 3-2 heading into the seventh at Progressive Field when Chase DeLauter's costly error in right field cracked open the door, and the Rays poured through it, plating three runs in the frame to take a lead they would never relinquish, winning 7-3 and squaring the best-of-seven series at two games apiece.

Junior Caminero, Yandy Diaz and Jonathan Aranda carried the offensive load for Tampa Bay, combining to go 6-for-14 with five RBIs in the victory. Diaz and Osleivis Diaz each went deep, both sluggers connecting for their first home runs of this postseason. Diaz also doubled, and Caminero added a two-bagger of his own as the Rays finished with 14 men left on base but did their damage when the moment demanded it most. Winning pitcher N. Martinez kept Cleveland's lineup in check long enough to hand Tampa Bay the lead for good.

Cleveland drew first blood in the opening inning and held a 3-2 advantage through six, but the Guardians' bullpen and defense unraveled in the seventh, when the Rays pushed across three runs before adding two insurance tallies in the ninth. Steven Palacios and Taylor Walls each stole a base as Tampa Bay's speed complemented its power. The series shifts with the clubs now deadlocked, and Game 5 looms with all the pressure squarely back on a Cleveland club that has now dropped back-to-back games at home.

story.headline: DYBANTSA ANKLE SCARE CLOUDS WIZARDS' OUTLOOK AS KNICKS, SIXERS MAKE ROSTER MOVES BEFORE OPENER
story.deck: The No. 1 pick exits Washington's preseason finale hurt while two teams reshape their frontcourts.
story.body:
WASHINGTON -- AJ Dybantsa, the 18-year-old phenom selected first overall by the Washington Wizards in the 2026 NBA Draft, limped off the court during the team's preseason finale after landing awkwardly on his left ankle, throwing the franchise's Opening Night plans into immediate uncertainty. Dybantsa did not return and was seen in a walking boot postgame, though the team offered no timetable for his return. The former BYU standout had been electric through the preseason, averaging 19.4 points and drawing comparisons to franchise cornerstones of Wizards teams past, making Sunday's injury all the more deflating for a fanbase starved for star power.

In New York, the Knicks made a pair of calculated roster decisions ahead of their regular-season opener, waiving guard Bruce Brown while retaining seven-foot center James Wiseman. Brown, a versatile defender who had battled to make the squad through training camp, was released as the front office opted for Wiseman's size and rim protection off the bench. Head coach Tom Thibodeau has long valued physicality in his rotations, and Wiseman's length gives New York a changeup option behind starting center Karl-Anthony Towns.

Philadelphia, meanwhile, took a long look at its injury-ravaged frontcourt and made a pragmatic call, converting seven-foot-six center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract. The 76ers, already thin up front with Joel Embiid managing his chronic knee issues, needed a credible insurance option capable of protecting the paint. Fall, who turns 31 in December, offers little offensive upside but provides a physical presence that can disrupt shot attempts and give opponents pause in the lane. The move underscores how fragile Philadelphia's roster construction remains heading into what the organization hopes will be a bounce-back season.

story.headline: HURRICANES ROLL TO SEVENTH STRAIGHT, AVALANCHE'S LEHKONEN PUTS FLYERS ON ICE
story.deck: Carolina's win streak hits seven games while Colorado's Finnish winger stays red-hot
story.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes carried a seven-game winning streak into Sunday's matchup against the Calgary Flames, arriving as the hottest team in the Metropolitan Division at 7-1-1. Calgary, meanwhile, limped in at 1-6, making the pairing one of the starkest mismatches of the young season. The Hurricanes have not lost a regulation game since their opening week, and their Metropolitan rivals are taking notice.

In Philadelphia, Artturi Lehkonen provided the marquee individual performance of the weekend, potting two goals as the Colorado Avalanche defeated the Flyers. Colorado improves to 5-2-1 on the season while Philadelphia continues to struggle at 1-6-3, the worst record in the Metropolitan Division. Lehkonen's two-goal effort gives the Avalanche a boost heading into what figures to be a bruising stretch of games.

Elsewhere around the league, the Pittsburgh Penguins carried a losing streak into Sunday's date with the surging Utah Mammoth, who sit at 6-3 in the Central Division. The Columbus Blue Jackets, fresh off an overtime victory that lifted them to 3-3, faced the Minnesota Wild, who have been one of the Central Division's steadiest performers at 5-2-1. Toronto, meanwhile, took a losing streak to San Jose, where the Sharks have posted a respectable 4-3-1 mark on home ice this season.

story.headline: QUARTERBACKS ON THE MOVE AS NFL OFFSEASON RESHAPES THE LEAGUE
story.deck: Several franchises overhauled their rosters this spring with bold trades and record signings.
story.body:
The NFL landscape looks dramatically different heading into the summer of 2026, with quarterback movement dominating the offseason conversation from coast to coast. The Cleveland Browns made the most aggressive push, acquiring veteran signal-caller Sam Darnold from the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a package of draft picks, betting on a fresh start for a franchise that has cycled through starters for years. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders signed free agent quarterback Justin Fields to a three-year, $112 million contract, giving the perpetually restless franchise a young arm they hope can anchor the offense for the next decade.

The 2026 NFL Draft in late April added more fuel to the rebuilding fires burning across the league. The Tennessee Titans, holding the first overall pick after a dismal 2025 campaign, selected Colorado defensive end Mason Holt, doubling down on an edge-rushing corps that was among the league's worst last season. The New York Giants used their second-round selection on Alabama wide receiver Darius Calloway, pairing him with their young quarterback and signaling a commitment to rebuilding the offense from the skill positions outward.

Training camps remain weeks away, but the storylines are already stacking up. The Dallas Cowboys, coming off a second consecutive early playoff exit, restructured the contracts of wide receiver CeeDee Lamb and linebacker Micah Parsons to free cap space, then splashed on offensive lineman help by signing guard Damien Lewis away from the Seattle Seahawks. In New England, first-year head coach Mike Vrabel continues installing his defensive system with a revamped secondary, raising expectations in Foxborough for the first time in several years.
